source: ModelStack skill · artificialanalysis.ai leaderboards + vendor pricing pages
note: Regenerate with the ModelStack skill (workflows/refresh_stack.md) — runs in Claude Code on the Max plan, costs no API credits. Treat anything older than 30 days as a hypothesis.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.why_best: Cheapest model that still summarises cleanly, and it emits noticeably fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash — which is the number that actually shows up on the bill.
models.use_when: Any bulk reading or digest-shaped work where volume drives cost.
models.avoid_when: The summary feeds straight into writing in your voice — switching vendors mid-pipeline costs you tone.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.why_best: Keeps the whole pipeline in one vendor when the summary is an input to drafting rather than an end product.
models.use_when: Summary → draft in one chain, no vendor handoff.
models.avoid_when: Summarising hundreds of items, where the price gap compounds.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.why_best: Roughly 10× cheaper than anything else usable, which is what makes hundreds-of-items summarising viable at all.
models.use_when: DailyDigest-shaped work: many items, low stakes per item.
models.avoid_when: Anything where a subtle misread matters.

summarize.gonzalo_tip: DailyDigest is exactly the shape DeepSeek V4 Flash is priced for — at $0.14/1M the whole feed costs less than one Opus call. Save the good model for the three items you actually read.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.why_best: Tops both writing boards, and is the only model where paying 2× Opus 5 for the same index score is defensible — because here the writing itself is the product.
models.use_when: Content posts, cover letters, scripts, world bibles — anything where voice is the deliverable.
models.avoid_when: Everything else. At $10/$50 it is not a general-purpose model.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.why_best: Same house voice at a fifth of Fable's price during the intro window.
models.use_when: Drafts, second passes, and volume writing.
models.avoid_when: The final pass on something with your name on it.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.why_best: Fast enough to iterate on structure in real time.
models.use_when: Outlines, section ordering, structural passes.
models.avoid_when: Final voice. Never let Haiku write the sentence that ships.

write.gonzalo_tip: Fable 5 is included in Claude Max at ~50% usage limits — so long-form writing you trigger yourself should run through Claude Code, not the API. That is $0 marginal instead of $10/$50.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.why_best: The strongest attested multilingual writer, which matters because @gonzabuilds ships in Spanish.
models.use_when: Spanish posts, captions, and hooks.
models.avoid_when: English long-form, where Fable 5 clearly leads.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.why_best: Plausibly equal or better for voice — but there is no public benchmark for Spanish or LatAm-Spanish quality anywhere, so this is a proxy, not a measurement.
models.use_when: English content, and as the A/B challenger for Spanish.
models.avoid_when: You need the cheap option — this is the premium tier.

models.name: Qwen 3.7 Max
models.why_best: Value tier for multilingual drafting when volume matters more than polish.
models.use_when: Bulk caption and hook variants.
models.avoid_when: The post that carries the week.

content.gonzalo_tip: There is no Spanish-quality leaderboard anywhere — every ranking here is a multilingual proxy. Run the same three real ES posts through Fable 5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, read them side by side, and pick. That 20 minutes beats any leaderboard.
content.source: AA multilingual proxies — no per-language ES benchmark exists

models.name: Nano Banana 2
models.why_best: Holds identity across a multi-reference series, which is exactly the carousel and storyboard job — and it scores higher than Nano Banana Pro at half the price.
models.use_when: Carousels, storyboards, any series that must look like one set.
models.avoid_when: The image contains real text you cannot proofread.

models.name: GPT Image 2
models.why_best: Near-perfect multilingual text rendering, and the only model that reliably puts legible words inside an image.
models.use_when: Cover images and thumbnails with typography in them.
models.avoid_when: Volume work — at $211/1k this is a cover tool, not a workhorse.

models.name: Reve 2.1
models.why_best: The value outlier of the entire board: 9× cheaper than GPT Image 2 and only 40 Elo behind it.
models.use_when: High-volume generation where each image is disposable.
models.avoid_when: Series consistency matters — that is Nano Banana 2's job.

models.name: MAI-Image-2.5-Flash
models.why_best: Cheapest credible option for instruction-based editing at volume.
models.use_when: Template work: same layout, one element swapped, many times.
models.avoid_when: First-generation quality matters more than turnaround.

images.gonzalo_tip: If you change one thing this month, change this: Nano Banana 2 outscores Nano Banana Pro at half the price. Also retire anything still pointing at FLUX.1 Kontext — it has fallen to Elo 1091 (#50) and the family is legacy.
images.source: AA Image Arena + Editing Arena, Jul 26 2026

models.name: ElevenLabs Scribe v2
models.why_best: Best hosted word error rate on the board, with word-level timestamps and SRT/VTT export built in.
models.use_when: Transcription you will cut video against.
models.avoid_when: Meeting recordings — AssemblyAI's diarization is worth more than the 0.9pt WER gap.

models.name: ElevenLabs v3
models.why_best: Most expressive TTS with audio tags and voice cloning, and the consensus pick for natural LatAm-Spanish narration — though no per-language Elo exists to prove it.
models.use_when: Narration and EN↔ES dubbing where the voice carries the piece.
models.avoid_when: A human is waiting on the audio — it is no longer the latency leader.

models.name: Cartesia Sonic 3.5
models.why_best: Outscores ElevenLabs v3 on blind preference and answers in under 90ms.
models.use_when: Anything realtime — voice agents, live coaching, interactive demos.
models.avoid_when: Maximum expressiveness matters more than latency.

models.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
models.why_best: Runs on your Windows laptop at ~900× realtime for nothing, which makes bulk and private footage free to process.
models.use_when: Bulk footage, anything private, anything you would rather not upload.
models.avoid_when: You need diarization or best-in-class accuracy.

audio.gonzalo_tip: For the UGBA 209 coach the cascade is still right — Scribe v2 Realtime → Claude → Sonic 3.5. Keep the architecture, just refresh the endpoints. And run bulk montage footage through Parakeet locally: 900× realtime, $0.

models.name: Gemini Omni Flash
models.why_best: Tops both video arenas with native audio and is the cheapest of the top tier — the 10s/720p cap is the only reason not to use it.
models.use_when: Any shot that fits in 10 seconds at 720p.
models.avoid_when: You need longer takes or 2K.

models.name: Seedance 2.0
models.why_best: 240 Elo above Kling 2.6 at roughly the same price, with ~95% character consistency claimed.
models.use_when: Longer takes or 2K output. Available on fal and Replicate.
models.avoid_when: A 10s 720p shot would do — Omni Flash is cheaper and scores higher.

models.name: Kling 3.0 1080p Pro
models.why_best: Not the value pick on price — the pick when you need the one thing it uniquely does: motion transfer from a reference video, plus Elements 3.0 subject binding.
models.use_when: Real basketball footage should drive the animation.
models.avoid_when: Generic generation — it is beaten on Elo and price everywhere else.

models.name: LTX-2.3 Fast
models.why_best: Cheapest usable draft renderer on the board, open weights, with native audio.
models.use_when: Previews and blocking passes.
models.avoid_when: Finals. Never render a final here.

video_gen.gonzalo_tip: WhatIfStudios runs Kling 2.6 Pro today at Elo 988 — Seedance 2.0 is 240 Elo higher at roughly the same price. That is the single biggest quality jump available to you right now. Also: Sora 2's API sunsets Sep 24 2026, so anything pointing at it needs to move.

models.name: Descript
models.why_best: Editing by deleting words in a transcript is the fastest path from raw talking-head footage to a cut, and filler/silence removal is automatic.
models.use_when: Long-form talking head and podcast-shaped footage.
models.avoid_when: Heavily visual edits that were never about the words.

models.name: Opus Clip
models.why_best: Turns one long video into ranked short candidates with auto-reframe, which is the whole repurposing step in one tool.
models.use_when: Long video → Reels/Shorts/TikTok cutdowns.
models.avoid_when: You already know which moment you want — the scoring adds nothing.

models.name: CapCut Pro
models.why_best: Covers beat sync and bilingual captions at the lowest price of anything here.
models.use_when: @gonzabuilds ES/EN repurposing on a budget.
models.avoid_when: You need transcript-level editing.

models.name: ElevenLabs Dubbing
models.why_best: Clones your voice across languages, which is the only way one recording serves both channels.
models.use_when: One take, two languages.
models.avoid_when: The Spanish version deserves its own performance.

video_edit.gonzalo_tip: The full creator stack (Descript + Opus Clip + ElevenLabs + Submagic) runs ~$77/mo. For @gonzabuilds specifically, CapCut + ElevenLabs dubbing covers ES↔EN repurposing at a fraction of that — start there and only add tools when a specific step actually hurts.

models.name: Claude Code on Opus 5
models.why_best: Best model on the best harness — and Terminal-Bench 2.1 shows the harness matters as much as the model.
models.use_when: Essentially all of your building. Run it through the Max subscription.
models.avoid_when: Mechanical bulk edits where Haiku is 5× cheaper per point.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.why_best: Tops Terminal-Bench on the Claude Code harness and is the established escalation target for brutal refactors.
models.use_when: The hardest 5–10% — gnarly refactors and debugging that Opus 5 stalls on.
models.avoid_when: Ordinary edits. It burns Max limits at ~2× the rate.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.why_best: Claude Code's default and correct for ordinary edits.
models.use_when: Day-to-day changes with a clear spec.
models.avoid_when: Cost-modelling off the sticker price — its new tokenizer emits ~30% more tokens for the same text, so the intro discount is smaller than it looks.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.why_best: Cheapest model per solved benchmark point on the whole board.
models.use_when: Small edits, loops, mechanical changes.
models.avoid_when: Anything requiring a plan.

code.gonzalo_tip: This is the one that matters for your wallet: run coding through Claude Code on the Max subscription, not the API. Same model, $0 marginal, and no prepaid balance to run dry mid-session — which has already blocked three of your projects.
code.source: Vals AI SWE-bench Verified + Terminal-Bench 2.1, Jul 26 2026

models.name: Voyage 4
models.why_best: One shared vector space across all three sizes, so you can index with voyage-4-large and query with voyage-4-lite — best-quality index at a sixth of the query cost.
models.use_when: Any RAG build. 200M free tokens, batch ~33% off.
models.avoid_when: You need open weights or fully local.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.why_best: The orchestration layer, not the embedding layer — it leads the agentic and tool-driving boards.
models.use_when: Agents, evals, multi-step orchestration.
models.avoid_when: Bulk scoring steps — that is Flash-Lite's job.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.why_best: Lowest latency measured anywhere, which is what you want for the scoring and routing steps inside a pipeline.
models.use_when: CareerOS job scoring, dedupe, tagging, routing — every 'score these 200 rows' step.
models.avoid_when: The step requires judgement rather than classification.

models.name: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
models.why_best: Runs on the laptop and 64.34 is plenty for a personal corpus.
models.use_when: Personal/private corpora, offline indexing.
models.avoid_when: You have a GPU — Qwen3-Embedding-8B scores 70.58 under Apache 2.0.

ai_ml.gonzalo_tip: Do not default to OpenAI embeddings — that is a 2024 habit and the line hasn't moved; text-embedding-3-large is now behind and OpenAI never shipped a v4. Also check chunk sizes before committing to gemini-embedding-001: its max input is 2,048 tokens vs Voyage's 32K.

models.name: GPT-5.6
models.why_best: The best general explainer on the board right now — strongest at meeting you where your understanding actually is.
models.use_when: First pass on an unfamiliar concept.
models.avoid_when: You want the explanation tied to code you are actually writing.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.why_best: Highest-scoring model on the index and already paid for through Max, so the marginal cost of asking is nothing.
models.use_when: Anything tied to your own repo, notes, or curriculum.
models.avoid_when: Nothing, really — this is your default.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.why_best: Free and fast enough to be the third opinion.
models.use_when: Quick checks and the disagreement test below.
models.avoid_when: Depth matters.

learn.gonzalo_tip: For a genuinely hard topic the highest-value move isn't the model — it's asking two different models the same question and reading where they disagree. That disagreement is almost always exactly the thing you don't understand yet. Worth doing on M04 ML and M06 Transformers especially.
